c.tagline: Where Spanish colonial history meets sprawling modern megacity energy.

taxi.fareNote: Insist on the meter; airport and mall taxis sometimes push flat/fixed rates instead - Grab is often more reliable and transparent on price.

emergency.note: 911 is the national emergency hotline covering police, fire, and medical.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Caution in Tondo, parts of Quiapo/Divisoria and Malate at night; drink-spiking and taxi scams — hide valuables.

hood_desc: High-rise financial and lifestyle district with malls, nightlife, and international dining; suits business travelers and those wanting comfort and safety.
Historic walled Spanish colonial city with churches and museums; suits history buffs and budget travelers, best visited by day.
Bayfront district with the Mall of Asia, casinos, and convention centers; suits families, event-goers, and casino visitors.
Upscale planned business district with skyscrapers, parks, and a vibrant food scene; suits travelers wanting a modern, walkable, safe base.
Historic district near Manila Bay with the US Embassy, Rizal Park, and colonial-era buildings; suits budget travelers wanting central access and bay sunsets.
lodging: Patio de Conchita Bed and Breakfast

water.note: Avoid tap water; use bottled or filtered water even though some areas claim treated supply.

transit.pay: Most rail lines use the Beep contactless stored-value card, tappable at turnstiles and reloadable at stations; jeepneys and buses are still largely cash-only with fares paid to the driver or conductor.
transit.hours: Rail lines generally run about 4:30/5am to 10-11pm; no regular overnight service, so Grab or taxis are used late at night.
transit.note: Traffic congestion is severe, so rail (LRT/MRT) is often faster than road transport during peak hours despite crowding.

airport.name: Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL)
airport.drive: 20-45 min depending on traffic and terminal

transit.m: P2P airport bus to Makati/Ortigas (45-90 min)

tip.r: 10% service charge often already included in restaurant bills; additional tipping is appreciated but not obligatory.
